Description: This Bauhaus HiFi rack 'Z125' by Artur Drozd offers space for approximately 500 vinyl records within a clear design language. The open shelving structure of chrome-plated steel tube and veneered blockboard organises storage across three generous shelves, connected by a central divider. The black surfaces contrast with the chrome frame, creating a graphic effect that draws on the functionalist Bauhaus tradition. Compact castors on the underside allow the unit to be repositioned freely at any time. The matt finish is particularly popular amongst customers. Zeitwerk Home manufactures this piece in their own Berlin workshop. Material, wood type, colour, dimensions and surface finish can be individually specified. At 150 cm wide, 40 cm deep and 98 cm tall, the HiFi rack suits the living room as well as a studio or study. Artur Drozd interprets the Bauhaus design language independently and adapts it to contemporary requirements.

Item Name: 1930s Art Deco Bar Cabinet with Walnut Veneer
Description: This Art Deco bar cabinet from the 1930s features a front of warm walnut veneer with lively grain, finished with hand-polished shellac for a rich lustre. The side panels are stained black, creating a clear contrast with the lighter wood tone of the front. Two chrome-plated handles provide subtle accents. The upper section conceals a bar compartment behind a lockable drop-down door. The lower part offers a view through glass sliding doors into a display compartment with a glass shelf, suited to glassware or decorative objects. The geometric design language and narrow plinth are typical of French Art Deco furniture from the interwar period. At 71 cm wide, 38 cm deep and 137 cm tall, this bar cabinet fits comfortably into narrower living spaces. In the dining room or living room, it works as a distinctive standalone piece that combines storage and display within a compact body. The piece originates from France and is in excellent condition.

This Bauhaus desk pedestal 'Z430' in beech was designed by Artur Drozd and manufactured by Zeitwerk Home in Berlin. The body of beech-veneered blockboard is oiled, revealing a warm, natural wood surface. A continuous chrome-plated steel tube frame encloses the body and gives the pedestal its characteristic cantilever form. Three drawers with stainless steel handles offer organised storage for office supplies and documents. The top is coated with linoleum, providing a robust and easy-care work surface. At 44 cm wide, 40 cm deep and 62 cm tall, the pedestal slides beneath virtually any desk. Material, wood type, colour and dimensions can be adapted to individual requirements. In the study or home office, this Bauhaus pedestal complements desks in the same style or sets an independent accent within modern interiors. Artur Drozd reinterprets the functionalist approach of the Bauhaus movement and adapts it to today's working life.

This Bauhaus desk 'Z420' by Artur Drozd combines clear lines with practical generosity. The linoleum work surface sits on a beech-veneered blockboard top, sealed with hard oil. Warm beech edges frame the grey linoleum surface and create a material contrast with the chrome-plated steel tube frame, which supports the desk in two characteristic loops. A central drawer provides space for pens and notes without interrupting the reduced design language. At 160 cm wide and 80 cm deep, the work surface allows concentrated work with ample freedom of movement. The working height of 75 cm meets ergonomic requirements. Zeitwerk Home manufactures this desk in their own Berlin workshop. Material, wood type, colour, dimensions and surface finish can be individually configured. In the study or office, this Bauhaus desk sets a clear design accent that works equally well with modern and classic interior styles.

This Bauhaus loop table 'Z417' by Artur Drozd consists of chrome-plated steel tube and lacquered glass. Two round surfaces of different diameters create a tiered silhouette that keeps the view open and lends the table a light presence. The upper glass top has a diameter of 75 cm, the lower measures 56 cm. Both are lacquered in black and reflect light subtly. The steel tube frame forms three loops that support the table and simultaneously define its design character. The chrome-plated surface corresponds with the dark glass tops, producing a material-driven contrast. At a height of 71 cm, the loop table serves as a side table in the living room or a surface beside the sofa. Zeitwerk Home manufactures this piece in their own Berlin workshop. Material, dimensions and the glass colour can be customised on request. Artur Drozd draws on the Bauhaus design language and translates it into an independent, functional form for contemporary living spaces.

Item Name: 1930s Bauhaus Chair by Mart Stam in Dove Blue
Description: This Bauhaus cantilever chair by Mart Stam from the 1930s displays the form that defined Czechoslovakian furniture production of that decade. The seat and backrest consist of shaped beech plywood, high-gloss lacquered in RAL 5014 dove blue. The chrome-plated steel tube frame traces the characteristic cantilever curve, producing a lightly sprung seating position. The smooth lacquered surface reflects light and gives the chair a cool, graphic presence. Mart Stam's design was manufactured in large quantities by various producers during the 1930s. This example is finished in dove blue. Further colour variants are available on request. At 39 cm seat width, 50 cm depth and 82 cm overall height with a 45 cm seat height, this Bauhaus chair suits the dining table, the study or as an accent chair in the living area. The piece originates from the Czech Republic and is in excellent condition.
